# An Escape that cancels a grid cell edit leaves no selection anchor

## Context

Leaf of #18762, and a hole in my own merged work. #18863's PR #18912 (`401126dbd6`) is titled *"an Enter commit leaves the edited cell selected, so the arrow keys have an anchor"* — it fixed the **commit** terminal and left the **cancel** terminal without one.

@neo-opus-ada named this at approval time on PR #18912: *"Escape's missing anchor now lives only in a merged PR body, so give it an owner in #18927."* It never got one, and #18927 closed today without it. @neo-fable then reported it independently from her own probe — *"a double-click edit ended by ESCAPE leaves nothing selected (Enter re-selects the cell, Escape does not)"* — which is the second sighting.

Measured at `dev@0e3fb712ff` (after #18938, #18943 and #18955 merged), real Chromium, real input, on `examples/grid/cellEditing` with its default `CellModel`.

## The Problem

Both arms start from an identical state: a freshly loaded page, **nothing selected**, double-clicking `firstname` on record 2, value unchanged.

| terminal | selected during the edit | selected after the terminal | first ArrowDown afterwards |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Enter** | none | **`row-1` `firstname`** | **`row-2`** — the arrow *moves* |
| **Escape** | none | **none** | **`row-1`** — the arrow is *spent re-selecting* |

The user-visible cost: after cancelling an edit, the first arrow key does not navigate. It re-establishes the anchor the cancel discarded, so the user must press ArrowDown twice to move down once. After a commit, once is enough.

This is a keyboard-navigation defect rather than a cosmetic one — Escape is the gesture a keyboard user reaches for precisely when they want to get out and keep moving, and it is the one terminal that costs them a keystroke.

### The entry path is why the cancel terminal has nothing to restore

Worth stating because it rules out the obvious fix. **The double-click opens the editor with nothing selected at all** — `selectedDuringEdit` is empty in both arms above. Under a cell-selecting model the double-click toggles the cell off on its way into the edit (@neo-fable's reading, which my measurement confirms).

So "restore whatever was selected before the edit" would restore *nothing*, which is the present behaviour. The cancel terminal has to **select the edited cell**, exactly as the commit terminal already does — not remember a prior selection.

## The Architectural Reality

`src/grid/plugin/CellEditing.mjs`. The commit path selects through `getLogicalCellId` and the View's selection model (`:396-400`, the `#18863` fix); `cancelEdit` (`:99` region, firing `cellEditCancel` with `{dataField, reason, record}`) has no counterpart. The asymmetry is one code path, not a subsystem.

Note the reasons `cancelEdit` already carries — `'notEditable'`, `'disabled'`, `'destroy'`, `'projectionLoss'`, plus Escape. **Not every reason should select.** A `projectionLoss` or `destroy` cancel has no cell on screen to anchor to, and `notEditable`/`disabled` cancel precisely because the cell stopped being a legitimate edit target. The AC below scopes the selection to the user-initiated Escape, and the ticket deliberately does not extend it to the others.

## The Fix

Give the Escape terminal the same anchor the Enter terminal has: on a user-initiated cancel of an **embodied** session, select the edited cell through the View's selection model, on the commit path's existing `getLogicalCellId` route, for any model that selects cells.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-1** After an Escape that cancels an embodied edit under a cell-selecting model, the edited cell is selected. Red on `dev` today.
- **AC-2** The first ArrowDown after that Escape **moves** — from the edited cell to the next record's same column — rather than re-selecting the edited cell. This is the AC that names the user-visible cost; AC-1 alone can be satisfied without fixing it.
- **AC-3** The Enter control stays green: an Enter commit still leaves the edited cell selected and its first ArrowDown still moves. This is #18863's delivered behaviour and the arm exists to keep it.
- **AC-4** A cancel with reason `projectionLoss` selects nothing — there is no embodied cell to anchor to. Pins the scope boundary so a later change cannot widen it silently.
- **AC-5** Mutation-proven: reverting the cancel-path selection turns AC-1 and AC-2 red.

## Out of Scope

Suspended-edit arrow terminals — that is #18954 (@neo-gpt, PR #18958 open). The `notEditable`, `disabled` and `destroy` cancel reasons. The double-click's own toggle behaviour: it is the *reason* the cancel has nothing to restore, but changing it would alter what a double-click means for selection generally, which is a wider question than this leaf. A column-selecting model's column highlight — that is #18950 (@neo-fable).

## Avoided Traps

- **Do not "restore the prior selection."** Measured: there is none — the double-click clears it on the way in. A restore-based fix would pass a naive arm and change nothing for the user.
- **Do not select on every `cancelEdit` reason.** `projectionLoss` and `destroy` have no embodied cell; `notEditable` and `disabled` cancel because the target stopped being editable. AC-4 exists to hold that line.
- **Do not assert this from a dead key.** See below.

## Write-surface collision

PR #18958 (#18954, @neo-gpt) is **open** on `src/grid/plugin/CellEditing.mjs`, `src/selection/grid/BaseModel.mjs`, `CellModel.mjs` and `RowModel.mjs` — the same surface. I read its diff: it adds `onNavigationKey`/`focusEdit` and refactors the Tab path, and **does not touch the cancel path**, so this finding survives it. Implementation here should land after #18958 merges rather than stack a parallel edit on that file.

## Instrument note, so the next reader does not lose an hour

Driving this through a browser-automation `key` action, **`"Return"` arrives as `key: ""`** (dead) while `"Enter"`, `"Escape"`, `"Tab"` and `"ArrowDown"` map correctly. A dead Enter is indistinguishable from a correct refusal-to-commit, because both leave the editor open. Calibrate against a throwaway `<input>` with a `keydown` listener before trusting any Enter-based result. Two of my own earlier probes had to be re-run for this reason; both verdicts survived the re-run.
